title: 2024 Bum Bowl
dek: The 2024 Bum Bowl was the two-week consolation final of the Buckaroo Football League's second season, in which Dawgs (Mekhi) defeated Ben Dover (Sonny) 243.8 to 210.46 over NFL weeks 17 and 18, sending Ben Dover to a second consecutive last-place finish.
body: The 2024 Bum Bowl decided last place in the six-team Buckaroo Football League, with the loser finishing sixth of six. It was played as a two-week aggregate over NFL weeks 17 and 18 of the 2024 season. The game ran opposite Buckaroo Bowl II, won that year by Habibsters (Kaushal) for the league's second straight title.

Dawgs, managed by Mekhi, entered as the 5 seed after a 5-9 regular season in which the team scored 1,413.5 points. Ben Dover, managed by Sonny, was the 6 seed, also at 5-9 but with 1,304.3 points, 109.2 fewer than the Dawgs. Identical records separated by a sizable scoring gap suggested that Kai's team had been the somewhat unluckier of the two, and Sonny's the somewhat luckier.

The two teams met three times in the regular season. Ben Dover won the first, 117.44 to 104 in week 2, after which the Dawgs took control of the series: 121.94 to 66.04 in week 7 and 96.46 to 44.1 in week 12, the latter one of the lowest totals of the season. Neither manager had won a Buckaroo Bowl entering the game.

The matchup carried extra history for Sonny, whose Ben Dover had finished last in the league's inaugural 2023 season. A loss would make him the league's only two-time last-place finisher, a distinction the league's founder and website builder was in no hurry to add to the record books.

The two finalists had already met once in the 2024 postseason. In the weeks 15-16 round, Ben Dover edged the Dawgs 253.22 to 247.24, a 5.98-point aggregate decision and the only earlier playoff meeting between these managers.

Ben Dover's win in that round was carried by running back Jonathan Taylor, who led the team with 49.4 points across the two weeks. For the Dawgs, quarterback Baker Mayfield was the top scorer with 50.3 points, but it was not enough to overcome Sonny's lineup.

The rematch in the Bum Bowl therefore offered Mekhi a chance to reverse the earlier result and Sonny a chance to complete a sweep of the postseason series, with the far less glamorous prize of simply not finishing last.
No in-game play-by-play exists for the 2024 Bum Bowl; the league site did not begin saving in-game events until week 7 of 2026. The summary below reflects weekly totals only.

Week 17: The Dawgs took a 126.4 to 115.7 lead after the first week, a margin of 10.7 points. Baker Mayfield led the way with 34.6 points, supported by Derrick Henry's 23.5 and 20 points from the Eagles D/ST. Ben Dover kept pace largely through Joe Burrow's 37-point week and Jonathan Taylor's 26.6, but got almost nothing from Rhamondre Stevenson (0.1), De'Von Achane (4.8) and Dalton Schultz (3.1). Both teams also played the week short-handed: the Dawgs started CeeDee Lamb and Kenneth Walker III, who were projected for zero and scored zero, and Ben Dover started kicker Evan McPherson under the same circumstances.

Week 18: Rather than closing the gap, Ben Dover lost ground. The Dawgs posted 117.4 points to Ben Dover's 94.8, winning the week by 22.6. Drake London delivered the decisive performance with 35.7 points, and Derrick Henry added 29.1, offsetting a quieter 21.6 from Mayfield and a scoreless week from A.J. Brown. Burrow fell to 13 points after his big week 17, and while Taylor (24.5), Achane (18.1) and the Ravens D/ST (17) all contributed, Ben Dover again drew nothing from Stevenson or McPherson.
The final aggregate was 243.8 to 210.46 in favor of the Dawgs, a margin of 33.3 points. Mekhi's side won both weeks and never trailed on the cumulative scoreboard.

Baker Mayfield led all scorers with 56.2 points against a two-week projection of 38.6, well above his season average of 15.6 points per start across eight starts. Derrick Henry added 52.6 points (projected 36.1), averaging 26.3 per week against his 16.3 per-start season mark. Drake London produced the biggest swing relative to expectation, scoring 49.8 against a projection of 24.3 and more than doubling his 10.5-point season average across the two weeks. The Eagles D/ST (27 points against a 14.3 projection) and kicker Chase McLaughlin (23 against 18.3) also beat expectations, the latter giving the Dawgs a Tampa Bay quarterback-kicker pairing that combined for 79.2 points.

For Ben Dover, Jonathan Taylor scored 51.1 points against a 38.9 projection, well above his season average of 11.5 per start, and Joe Burrow added 50 against 40.8. The Ravens D/ST was the team's most surprising contributor at 31 points, against a projection of 16.6 and a season average of just 4.7 per start. Amon-Ra St. Brown (26.7) and Garrett Wilson (21.2) finished slightly below projection.

The game's most notable flop was Rhamondre Stevenson, who was projected for 21.5 points and produced 0.1. Ben Dover also received zero points from its kicker slot, where McPherson was projected for nothing and delivered exactly that, and only 7.5 from tight end Dalton Schultz.

Ben Dover's bench told the story of the loss. Malik Nabers scored 47.5 points there, including 32.6 in week 17, a total that by itself exceeded the 33.3-point margin. Michael Pittman Jr. added 31.6 bench points, Aaron Rodgers 25.4 and George Kittle 18.9, the last of whom outscored Schultz by 11.4. The Dawgs left points behind too, with Marvin Harrison Jr. (27.4), Davante Adams (25), Breece Hall (22.5), Puka Nacua (17.9) and Terry McLaurin (17.2) all sitting while Lamb and Walker filled starting spots with zeroes, but Mekhi's starters produced enough that it did not matter.

The win lifted the Dawgs to a fifth-place finish and avenged their narrow weeks 15-16 loss to the same opponent, while also extending their 2024 head-to-head advantage over Ben Dover to three wins against two across the regular season and playoffs.

The loss consigned Ben Dover to sixth place for the second consecutive season, making Sonny the first manager in league history to finish last twice, both times with the same team name. It completed a full Bum Bowl tour of shame for the league's first two years and left the commissioner, the man who built the website hosting these standings, as the author of his own most unflattering entries.

The result later became the low point of one of the league's defining arcs. In 2025, Sonny's Ben Dover went 13-3 and won Buckaroo Bowl III, going from last place to champion in a single season. Mekhi's Dawgs, meanwhile, slid from fifth to last in 2025, so the two managers effectively traded places at opposite ends of the standings one year after this game.
